name: sta_lta
description: Recursive STA/LTA on cf = x*x, float32: s = fl(fl(d*s) + fl(c*cf)), c = 1.0f/N, d = 1.0f - c, s starts at 0; ratio = sta/lta (0 when lta <= 0). Trigger: no event while n < n_lta; then the ratio must be < ratio_on once before arming; armed: first n with ratio >= ratio_on is an onset, event [onset - n_pre, onset + n_post); refractory until n >= max(onset + n_post, onset + 1), then wait-low again. Invalid (lost) samples are skipped: no update, ratio 0, neither low nor high, the input value there is ignored; warm-up and refractory still count them (they are time). Input = the decimated, filtered clip. Sample indices are 64-bit (u64, D-018) in the firmware; they never wrap. The global index n and quiet_until (the refractory end) are int64/uint64. The trigger emits an event at its onset (no n_invalid). Every event is then reported once as a window with n_invalid = samples of [start, end) that are invalid, before index 0, or at or past the end of the stream (when the stream ends before end); the features stage skips windows with n_invalid > 0 and counts the skip. masked: the stream is input[:len(valid)] with that valid mask, and it ends there (the last window is cut).
build: Firmware builds the dsp/trigger sources with -ffp-contract=off (no fused multiply-add).

tolerance.note: on ratio, relative to max(|ratio|, 1), both cases = 10x the larger of the FMA-emulation and float64-reference errors; events and windows must match exactly (checked to hold under both).
